Judgment
Dated this the 8th day of April, 2025 The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No1289/2015 on the file of the Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode is the appellant herein.

entities.text: Principal Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: (For the purpose of convenience, the parties are hereafter referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal).

2. The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Sections 140 and 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 22.10.2014.

According to the petitioner, on 22.10.2014 at about 6.15 p.m., while he was riding a scooter, a car bearing registration No. KA 12 M 3083 owned by the 1st respondent and negligently driven by the 2 nd respondent hit against his scooter and as a result of the accident, the petitioner sustained serious injuries.
3.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the petitioner, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver 2025:KER:32668 of the offending vehicle.
The quantum of compensation claimed in the O.P. is Rs.10,00,000/-.
4. The insurance company filed a written statement, admitting the accident as well as policy, but disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
5. The evidence in the case consists of documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A17 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

sentences.text: After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal found negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, awarded a total compensation of Rs.4,10,440/- and directed the insurer to pay the same.
7. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

8. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable?

9. Heard Sri. R. Sudhish, the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri.
Thapas A Varma, the learned Standing 2025:KER:32668 Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
10.
The Point: In this case the accident as well as valid insurance policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
One of the contentions raised by the learned counsel for the petitioner is regarding the income of the petitioner as fixed by the Tribunal.
According to him, the petitioner was a Masters of Tourism Administration Student in Maharaja Tourism Development Institute, Mysore.
Exhibit A17 is the copy of Identity card issued from the said institute in favour of the petitioner.

She would also argue that the petitioner was a volleyball player and in order to substantiate the same she has relied upon Exhibit A16 certificate issued from Kendriya Vidhyalaya, Sangathan, which will go to show that he was a volleyball player also.
However, the Tribunal has fixed his notional income at Rs.2500/-, which is prima facie on the lower side.

11. As per the dictum laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the decision in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236], the notional income of a coolie, in the year 2014 will come to Rs.9500/-.

entities.text: Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the decision 2025:KER:32668 in Nanu K and Others v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. (MACA.565/2019), the notional income of a final year Engineering student was fixed by this Court in 2015 at a sum Rs.22,000/-.

entities.text: Nanu K and Others v. National Insurance Co. Ltd. (MACA.565/2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Madhusoodhanan and Others (MANU/KE/947/2022], the notional income of an Engineering graduate, involved in an accident of the year 2016, was fixed by this Court at Rs.20,000/-.

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Madhusoodhanan and Others (MANU/KE/947/2022]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the decision in Aswathy V. Ayoob and Another (MACA.No.2316/2016), the notional income of a B.Com. Graduate involved in an accident of the year 2011 was fixed by this Court at Rs.12,000/-.

Therefore, considering the fact that the petitioner was a MTA student and the accident was in the year 2014, his notional income is fixed at Rs.14,000/-.
12.

In the accident the petitioner sustained the following injuries:
"open fracture shaft of right femur, open fracture right tibia, proximal tibio-fibular syndesmotic injury, posterior dislocation hip right and abrasion on right elbow."
13.
The petitioner was treated as inpatient for 28 days in three spells.
In the meanwhile, he had under gone three surgeries also.

As per 2025:KER:32668 Exhibit C1 disability certificate issued by a Jeseel Sreyas vs Sarvesh M on 8 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157273666/
3
Doctor appointed by the Tribunal, the petitioner suffered 24% permanent physical disability.
The Tribunal, however, scaled down the percentage of disability of the petitioner to 12%, without assigning valid and cogent reasons.

The law is settled that, if the Tribunal is not satisfied with the disability certificate produced by the petitioner, the remedy is to refer him to a medical board or higher Authority.(See Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305).

entities.text: Manikantan G. v. Janardhanan Nair and Others, 2021 (5)KHC 305)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Having not done so, the Tribunal was not justified in scaling down the percentage of disability from what is shown in the disability certificate.

According to learned counsel for the petitioner, though an application was filed for examining the petitioner by a medical board, the Tribunal declined the same an appointed a single Doctor and accordingly Exhibit C1 was received.
I do find any grounds to disbelieve the said disability and as such the permanent physical disability of the petitioner is fixed as 24%.
14. On the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 23 years.

Therefore, 40% of the monthly income is to be added towards future 2025:KER:32668 prospects, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680] and the multiplier to be applied is 18, as held in Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121].

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd v. Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation, [(2009) 6 SCC 121]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, the loss of disability will come to Rs.10,16,064/-.
15. Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- and towards 'loss of amenities of life' Rs.15,000/- was awarded.

According to the learned counsel for the petitioner,
the compensation awarded on those heads are on the lower side.
Towards 'extra nourishment' no compensation was awarded.
16. The petitioner sustained serious injuries in the accident and was treated as inpatient for 28 days in three spells and in the meanwhile he had undergone three surgeries also.

Because of the injuries sustained, the percentage of disability suffered and the length of treatment undergone by the petitioner, I hold that the compensation awarded by the Tribunal on the heads 'pain and sufferings'
and 'loss of amenities of life' are on the lower side and hence they are enhanced to Rs.75000/-
2025:KER:32668 and Rs1,00,000/- respectively.
Similarly, the petitioner is also entitled to get Rs.10,000/- towards 'extra nourishment'.
Towards loss of study, the petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.42,000/-(14000x3).
17. No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.

18. Therefore, the petitioners/appellants are entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.15,16,298/-,
as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference:

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and Respondent No.3 is directed to deposit a total sum of Rs.15,16,298/- (Rupees fifteen lakh sixteen thousand two hundred and ninety eight only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest at the rate ordered by the Tribunal, from the date of the petition till deposit/realisation, excluding interest for a period of 192 days, the period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.

(Enhanced compensation will carry interest @8%).
20.
